name: @cg/web
//: `dev` and `start` go through `scripts/next.ts` so that PORT comes from this service's own `.env.local`, the way it does for the three Bun services. `next dev --port ${PORT:-3000}` did not: the shell expanded it before anything read the file, and the service bound 3000 in a worktree that owns 4410. See #50 and the comment at the top of that script; `test/dev-port.test.ts` fails if the shell-expanded form comes back.
//ws: `ws` is a transitive runtime dependency, declared here on purpose. `@mastra/core` opens it at module scope (`import WebSocket from "ws"`), and Bun's isolated install links only a package's *declared* dependencies — so without this line `ws` exists only under `node_modules/.bun/@mastra+core@…/node_modules/ws` and is unreachable from `apps/web`. In the Alpine builder webpack left it as a bare `require("ws")` external, Next's file tracing could not resolve that specifier from the emitted route, and the standalone image shipped without it: `POST /api/chat` answered `Cannot find module 'ws'` on Render while `next start` on a full node_modules was fine. Declaring it is the whole fix — the specifier now resolves from this package, so tracing carries it. Measured in #92; `scripts/verify-standalone.ts` is what proves it, against the Docker image rather than `next start`.
//gc: `@cg/governance-core` is a devDependency, not a dependency: nothing the deployed service renders or routes imports it. The one importer is `scripts/gateway-stand-in.ts`, a local fixture a forker deletes, which needs #9's `routeApproval` — the same module `tools/approvals` is checked against — so the offline run routes an escalation by the real rule rather than by a second copy of it. A dependency edge from the governed UI to the control plane's engine is exactly what this repo keeps refusing; a dev-only edge from a stand-in is not that.
